name: Companion
description: A coding agent you call up: hold ⌃⌥ in any app and speak (drag to draw), let go and it answers by your pointer. In a note, write @claude to ask it something, or @ and a name to start another (@opus, @codex, @opus-review): it answers in bubbles, comments on lines (cards in the margin), suggests changes you take with Tab, proposes larger ones you take change by change, or writes with you. Always-on sessions on this machine: Claude Code's run in the app (its chat), Codex's and OpenCode's in terminals.

mode.label: Mode

labels.pair: Pair: with you as you write

mode.description: how much it does: off; quiet, it answers only what you ask it (@claude in a note, Ask companion); pair, it also sees what you write when you pause, answers what's meant for it as a person in the room would, and may write in your notes

agent.label: Agent
agent.description: the coding agent its session runs (claude, codex, opencode, claude_personal...)

name.label: Name
name.description: what it's called, on its cursor and after @ in a note; empty: the agent's name (Claude, Codex)

model.label: Model
model.description: the model a new session runs (sonnet, opus, haiku, a full name) when its name picks none; Claude Code's (others run their own unless set). A quicker one answers sooner

effort.label: Effort
effort.description: how hard its model thinks (low, medium, high, xhigh, max) when its name picks none; Claude Code's (others run their own unless set). Less answers sooner

profiles.label: Names
profiles.description: what an @name starts, by its first part (@opus-review: opus): name: agent, then model and effort if not the defaults. Yours add to these, or change one by its name

comments.label: Comments
comments.description: where its comments and suggestions show: as cards beside the text, or in the Conversations panel (a dot by each one's line)

pause.label: Pause before it looks
pause.description: seconds without typing mid-sentence before it sees what you wrote (Pair); a sentence's end goes after a breath, Enter and a question at once

private.label: Private
private.description: what it never sees: a folder of notes (nothing you do there reaches it, nor does a note with companion: private in its properties), a site (site: bank.com, its subdomains too), a Browser container (container: <id>) or an app (app: <bundle id>, kept from it by the helper). Starts with password managers and banks

keys.label: Talk keys
keys.description: on a Mac, the keys that call it up at your pointer, in any app: hold one and speak (drag to draw on the screen), let go and it answers there; a tap opens a box to type in, a double tap listens hands-free until the next. These keys never dictate

fresh_after.label: Fresh session after
fresh_after.description: moments it handles before a fresh session takes over, told a short summary and its open threads, so its context stays small

prompt.default: You're the user's companion in Vaultite, the app where they keep their notes. Your cursor and your words show in their window as you act: you're a person in the room with them. First read ME.md (who they are, how they want you to work) and `vau docs companion`. When to speak: always answer an ask, a point (they pointed or drew at something without a word: look at it) or a reply. In pair mode you also see what they write: answer a question or a remark meant for you even without your @name, and stay silent while they write to themselves. When you can't tell, answer: a short bubble, or a short question (say with ask), which they can ignore. When you stay silent, pass with a few words why. Where words go: a bubble (say) is your voice, for answers in the moment, how something works, quick replies; the note gets content, what they'd want there tomorrow: ideas they asked for, a design, a list (edit, in pair mode or when asked). An accept or a reject needs no word back. They teach you: a bubble put in the note, an answer folded back into a bubble, a bubble dismissed. Take the hint, and keep a lasting preference with `vau remember --about preference`. Beyond notes: an ask can be about a terminal, a page, a tab or a panel, or another app on their screen; follow one only when they ask (follow), and offer to keep it as a watch. In their web page, act (act) when they'd want it, as in notes; long browsing goes to a page of your own.
prompt.label: Session prompt
prompt.description: what its always-on session is told when it starts (then how what you do reaches it: its messages, or a loop in its terminal)
